 1m ago 10.37 EDT Wolves go in front against Watford. Adam Armstrong gets the goal at Molinuex and Wolves currently sit fourth in the live league table behind Middlesbrough, Swansea and West Ham.
 Share 3m ago 10.36 EDT GOAL! West Ham 1-3 Southampton (Walker-Peters, 24 mins)
 There is another goal at the London Stadium but it’s the visitors again! Lewis Dobbin passes the ball into the net to restore Saints’ two-goal margin.
 Share 4m ago 10.35 EDT GOAL! Rangers 1-0 St Johnstone (Kelsy, 29 min)
 Kevin Kelsy breaks the deadlock at Ibrox. Rangers can pull within a point of leaders Celtic with victory today.
 Share 7m ago 10.32 EDT West Ham pushing for an equaliser against Southampton. Going 2-0 down after 11 minutes was a shock for the Hammers but they’re now forcing Southampton back again and again. Can the Saints reach half-time still in front?
 Share Updated at  10.32 EDT 8m ago 10.30 EDT More chances for Arsenal. Noni Madueke drags a great chance horribly wide when he should have at least tested Pickford. Then, a Rice dummy sets up a shooting chance for Merino but Everton block.
 Share 10m ago 10.28 EDT GOAL! West Ham 1-2 Southampton (Walker-Peters, 24 mins)
 West Ham hit back! Don’t rule out the Hammers just yet. Kyle Walker-Peters thumps home to cut Southampton’s lead in half. Three goals and not even 25 minutes on the clock.
 Share 13m ago 10.25 EDT Arsenal racking up the corners. That’s five so far. Everton have won just one of their last 30 away Premier League matches against Arsenal (D5 L24) by the way while David Moyes is winless in 13 league road trips against the Gunners.
 Share 17m ago 10.21 EDT Fulham within a whisker at Coventry. Still 0-0 but the visitors so close to breaking the deadline as Oscar Bobb finds Josh King, who smashes his shot off the woodwork.
 Share Updated at  10.23 EDT 19m ago 10.20 EDT Everton go close again. David Raya makes a mess of a punch after coming for a corner and Gabriel has to clear off the line.
 Share 20m ago 10.18 EDT Everton go close to an equaliser at Arsenal. The Toffees have responded well since going behind and Tyrique George curls an effort not far wide after his shot deflects off Ben White. Mikel Arteta looks agitated.
 Share 22m ago 10.16 EDT Richard Kone has a hat-trick for QPR! Just 15 minutes gone and Swansea, who had conceded just eight goals this season, are 3-0 down. Kone, by the way, hadn’t scored since April! Remarkable scenes at Loftus Road!
 View image in fullscreen Take a bow, Richard Kone! Photograph: Andrew Matthews/PA Share Updated at  10.31 EDT 24m ago 10.15 EDT GOAL! West Ham 0-2 Southampton (Bree, 11 mins)
 Wow! Southampton go 2-0 up at the London Stadium thanks to an absolute thunderblaster from James Bree. Middlesbrough must be loving this. Their two closest rivals, Southampton and Swansea, have the chance to overtake them at the top but the pair are both losing 2-0. And it could be about to get worse for Swansea…
 Share Updated at  10.26 EDT 26m ago 10.12 EDT Fantastic start for QPR against Swansea. The Swans have the chance to go top but QPR have struck twice in the opening 10 minutes, Richard Kone scoring both goals.
 Share 29m ago 10.10 EDT GOAL! Arsenal 1-0 Everton (Konsa, 7 mins)
 The Gunners are ahead! Well, maybe they do have their eyes on the 6-0 win that will take them top. After a run of corners, Pickford and Mykolenko get in a bit of a muddle and Konsa is there to force the ball home. A bit of a messy one but Arsenal won’t care. Does that count as their first set-piece goal of this Premier League season.
 View image in fullscreen Ezri Konsa pokes home his first goal for the Gunners! Photograph: Adam Davy/PA Share Updated at  10.18 EDT 32m ago 10.07 EDT At Arsenal, the pattern has already been set. The home side are on the attack, with Everton hoping to hit on the break. Gyokeres will be hoping to make the most of a rare start today and he almost gets in a the near post from an Eze cross but Jake O’Brien does well to turn the ball behind for a corner. But…
 Share 34m ago 10.04 EDT GOAL! West Ham 0-1 Southampton (Matsuki, 1 min)
 West Ham can go top with a win but their task is suddenly much harder. Southampton take the lead with just a minute on the clock.
 Share 37m ago 10.02 EDT Thanks Billy. Peeeeeep! Let’s go!
 Share 37m ago 10.01 EDT David Tindall is here to walk you through the first half.
 Share 38m ago 10.00 EDT Before kick-off, Arsenal pay tribute to their former managing director and life president Ken Friar , who died two weeks ago at the age of 92. Friar played a huge part in Arsenal’s move from Highbury to the Emirates, where there is a footbridge named after him and a statue of him as a boy outside. The rain is coming down and kick-off against Everton is next.
 Share 44m ago 09.54 EDT Before the 3pm games get under way , here are the starting lineups from the other game in the Premier League at the CBS Arena.
 Coventry (4-2-3-1): Rushworth; Van Ewijk, Thomas, Pinnock, Dasilva; Grimes, Yirenkyi; Sakamoto, Rudoni, Thomas-Asante; Cherif.
 Subs: Bentley, Mason-Clark, Mfuni, Awoniyi, Onyeka, Kesler-Hayden, Torp, Gboho, Hamer.
 Fulham (4-2-3-1): Leno; Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson; Larsson, Charles; Bobb, King, Iwobi; Garcia.
 Subs: Lecomte, Tete, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Cairney, Kevin, Berge, Manuel Angel.
 Share 48m ago 09.50 EDT Scotland: Simon McMahon welcomes us to a soggy, windswept Fitba Corner …
 “Currently in Frews Bar about to walk through a literal storm to Scotland’s game of the day at Tannadice, where Dundee United ‘welcome’ Aberdeen. After a tricky start to the season, United have started to click recently, with seven points from the last nine, thanks largely to midfield trio of Cameron, Iqbal and Tait pulling the strings. Though the wind and rain might suit Aberdeen more, so anything could happen ... Other games include Rangers v St Johnstone and St Mirren v Dundee.”
 Share 52m ago 09.47 EDT If they hop on a lime bike , those celebrating Arsenal Women fans in the away end at Tottenham might just make it to the Emirates for kick-off in the Premier League . The champions take on Everton knowing that the leader Manchester City have gone down to Aston Villa in the early kick-off. A 6-0 win will send them top – just saying.

 Share Updated at  09.49 EDT 1h ago 09.40 EDT WSL full-time: Tottenham 1-2 Arsenal
 Alessia Russo’s second-half penalty decides the north London derby and relieves some of the pressure on the Arsenal head coach, Renée Slegers, after five league games without a win. She will be pleased with how her side responded to going a goal down after Cathinka Tandberg’s headed opener, with Georgia Stanway hitting back just minutes later in the first half.
 Arsenal move up to 6th in the WSL, one point and two places behind Spurs, who have now lost three in a row. Manchester City lead the way with six wins out of six and face United in the derby tomorrow.

 Share 1h ago 09.33 EDT WSL: Seven minutes added on in the north London derby, with Arsenal still leading 2-1. Much of that was for the treatment for Alice Sombath’s serious-looking injury at the start of the half.

 Share Updated at  09.54 EDT 1h ago 09.28 EDT Ed Aarons at the Emirates Stadium 
 It’s a big day for Viktor Gyokeres as he makes his first Premier League start of the season after setting up Arsenal’s equaliser against Bayern Munich in midweek. The Sweden striker found the net 21 times last season but has yet to score for his club this season in nine appearances, albeit mainly as a substitute. With Bukayo Saka absent, Eberechi Eze comes in on the left flank and Noni Madueke is back on the right. Mikel Merino also makes a rare start in midfield on a rainy day in north London.
 Everton are without Jack Grealish due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is not in the squad due to concussion protocols. David Moyes’s side haven’t beaten Arsenal in their last seven meetings home or away and are winless at the Emirates since April 2021.
 Share 1h ago 09.26 EDT Arsenal v Everton team news
 Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Rice, Merino; Madueke, Odegaard, Eze; Gyokeres.
 Subs: Arrizabalaga, Mosquera, Hincapie, Timber, Havertz, Calafiori, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman.
 Everton (4-2-3-1): Pickford; Rohl, O’Brien, Tarkowski, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry.
 Subs: Travers, King, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Dibling, Norgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney, Graham.
 Share 1h ago 09.24 EDT WSL: We’re into the final 10 minutes at Spurs, who have thrown on winger Olivia Holdt for Summanen in an attacking change. Arsenal have withdrawn Catley for Elisa de Almeida in a defensive one.
 Share 1h ago 09.18 EDT WSL: Big chance for Arsenal to finish this off! Smith’s cross from the left is perfect for Baum to run and volley but the winger makes no contact with the ball whatsoever.
 Share 1h ago 09.16 EDT Championship: We have a couple of late goals in the second tier – Patrick Bamford has equalised for Sheffield Utd at home to Derby, that’s 1-1. And it’s chaos at Fratton Park as Millwall’s Jake Cooper clears the ball into Thomas Waddington to give Portsmouth a 2-1 lead.
